mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy cycle, lowering discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS rising consistently, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and returns falls below 0.3 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days, reflecting strengthening labor market conditions and increased economic confidence.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns fail to be significantly positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 4.5%, or the returns are not higher than baseline during this period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in demand (GDPC1) and monetary easing (FEDFUNDS) create a synergistic effect, amplifying equity valuation growth and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite both GDPC1 and FEDFUNDS rising, or the interaction effect (IC) between the proxies falls below 0.3 over a 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: An upward crossing of the supply index (INDPRO) above 100 triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days, indicating expanding production capacity and stronger economic growth potential.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns fail to be significantly positive (p > 0.05) when INDPRO crosses above 100, or the returns are not higher than baseline during this period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% during a late-cycle expansion regime signals potential tightening, but paradoxically, this may compress equity valuations temporarily, yet the 60-day forward returns remain positive due to delayed market adjustments.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5%, or the returns are lower than in non-tightening periods of similar magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in both demand (GDPC1) and labor employment (PAYEMS) above their recent trends triggers a short-term positive S&P 500 forward return within 5 trading days, reflecting immediate market optimism about economic growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and PAYEMS both rise above their 5-day moving averages
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns fail to be significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite both proxies rising above their moving averages, or the interaction effect (IC) between them is below 0.3 over the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in the supply index (INDPRO) and monetary easing (FEDFUNDS) create a reinforcing cycle that drives up equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite both INDPRO and FEDFUNDS rising, or the interaction effect (IC) between the proxies falls below 0.3 over a 3-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in labor employment (PAYEMS) above 136,000 triggers a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, signaling a robust labor market and sustained economic momentum.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns fail to be significantly positive (p > 0.05) when PAYEMS crosses above 136,000, or the returns are not higher than baseline during this period.
